units.text: Begin with the fleet definition on the left. Target capacity can combine Spot and optional On-Demand instances. Define eligible pools by instance type, operating system and Availability Zone, and use weights that express useful capacity units.

The upper middle panel shows price capacity optimized allocation. It considers pools with strong available capacity and then price. AWS recommends this strategy for most Spot workloads; it does not remove interruption risk.

The upper right panel shows capacity optimized allocation. It prioritizes pools with stronger available capacity to reduce near-term interruption risk. Capacity availability and the lowest current price are different selection criteria.

The diversified strategy spreads Spot capacity across the specified pools. Pool selection still needs instance compatibility, useful capacity weights and an application that can recover from interruption.

The lowest-price strategy prioritizes cheaper pools. AWS generally does not recommend it because interruption risk can be higher. A lower hourly price does not necessarily produce the lowest completed-work cost.

Return to the full slide and include the fleet manager in the decision. Spot Fleet is distinct from an Auto Scaling mixed-instances policy. Target capacity is a request, not a guarantee, and price or budget constraints can prevent fulfillment.
Start with DNS and delivery at the upper left. Route 53 resolves names, while CloudFront brings cacheable content closer to users. Name resolution and content delivery are separate responsibilities.

The upper right panel covers application ingress. Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer and API Gateway address different entry requirements. An Elastic IP is an address, not a load balancer.

Move to compute and caching. EC2 and Auto Scaling, Lambda, containers, Batch and EMR offer different execution models. ElastiCache and DynamoDB DAX can reduce repeated access when their consistency and data models fit.

The next row separates data services from messaging and workflows. Databases, search and analytics serve different access patterns. Queues, notifications, streams and workflow coordination decouple work or coordinate steps.

The lower-left panel adds storage. S3 storage classes, EBS, EFS and instance store have different access and durability models. Match each stateful component to the recovery and sharing behavior the application needs.

With the whole system visible, validate the connections between layers. Check security, dependencies, cost and failure behavior across the complete request and data path. Choosing an EC2 instance is only one part of solution architecture.
